goal: Improve attack-family holdout detection while measuring normal-task false positives separately.
first_experiment: Fit normal-only IsolationForest on the existing 26 bucket features. Keep the existing six-session split, normal-only calibration and target FPR 0.005. Compare first-two and all-four training sessions without test tuning.
completed_experiment: Both fixed normal-only models recorded TP0/FN134/FP1/TN254. No candidate was exported or deployed. Results: normal_only_evaluation_20261006.json.
completed_unlink_audit: All 23082 recorded attempts matched the 389 fixed test buckets, outside=0 and unknown_scope=0. Normal zip cleanup peaked at 8312 attempts versus ransom_sim 105 and wiper_sim 58. Amount and directory breadth alone are not a sufficient rule. Results: unlink_bucket_audit_20261006.json.
evidence_limits: The existing corpus has already been inspected. This comparison cannot establish blind unseen-attack efficacy or production FPR.

telemetry_audit.file_destruction: The accepted retest collector log records 23082 FILE_UNLINK events. detect2.py and the 31-feature aggregate currently do not use unlink-event counts or paths. Reuse these captured events before adding a new sensor. The hook records a basename with partial-path flags, not a full path. Scope counts use known device/directory-inode pairs and report unknown scope separately. An LSM unlink hook is an attempted operation, not proof that deletion succeeded.
telemetry_audit.rename: Current aggregate does not count rename operations. Syscall-enter events can count attempts, but without matching exits they do not prove success; names and affected path scope require additional instrumentation.
telemetry_audit.resource_abuse: Current aggregate includes syscall count and process count but no measured CPU runtime. Duration or syscall volume alone must not be labeled unauthorized resource use.
telemetry_audit.roles: Current six-session benchmark combines normal tasks in one training scope. It cannot validate separate cron, web, container and administrator baselines without new role-labeled normal captures. Role must come from independently configured workload identity, not a test technique label.

next_gate: Develop temporal continuity and independently configured role context for repeated file changes, retaining normal cleanup controls. Do not choose a duration threshold from the observed test attack lengths. CPU-runtime evidence is still absent. Freeze the next feature schema, score and calibration rule before collecting fresh validation data.

fresh_validation.training: Normal role-labeled workloads only for the anomaly model; keep administrator negative controls including bulk file maintenance and sustained compilation.
fresh_validation.calibration: Separate normal sessions, with no attack rows or test threshold adjustment.
fresh_validation.test: Fresh normal work and benign local dummy-file simulations from a family withheld from feature/model development. Never execute exploit or CVE payloads.
fresh_validation.quality: Reject incomplete units, ambiguous labels and event-loss sessions. Record optional metadata gaps separately.
fresh_validation.metrics: Bucket DR/FPR, incident-level detection and delay, repeat/sleep coverage, and quality counters; do not treat correlated buckets as independent incidents.
fresh_validation.promotion: Keep candidates offline until independent replay/input compatibility checks and fresh normal/held-out-family evaluation pass. Preserve V1 shadow and original detector.
